To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
highly recyclable dicarbolic acids are a low cost and green alternative to mineral acid for the production of thermally stable carboxylated cellulosic nanomaterials.
the dicarboxylated acid treatment is a green and low-cost method to produce high thermally stable carboxylated CNCs and CNFs from cellulosic biomass.

the use of highly recyclable dicacarboxylic acids in the production of CNCs and CNFs can result in higher carboxylic group content, higher thermal stability, and longer lengths of CNCs, as well as lower energy consumption and lower cellulose loss to sugar in CNFs, than mineral acid-based processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of green, low-cost, and highly recyclable cellulose nanomaterials from renewable resources.
the development of a potentially low cost and highly recyclable solid acid hydrolysis of cellulosic fibers to produce thermally stable and highly carboxylated CNCs and CNFs.
the production of carboxylated CNCs and CNFs using low-cost dicarboxyic acids as the hydrolysis agent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of highly recyclable dicarbolic acids for the production of thermally stable and highly carboxylated CNCs and CNFs is a green and cost-effective process.

dicarboxylica acids can be used to produce thermally stable and functional carboxylated CNCs and CNFs with high yields, low cellulose loss to sugar and minimal energy consumption, and that the resultant solid residues can be recycled to produce CNFs.
the solid acid hydrolysis of cellulosic materials is a promising green and low-cost method to produce high quality CNCs and CNFs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solid acids are a low cost, highly recyclable, and green alternative to mineral acids for cellulose nanomaterials (CNM) production.
the use of solid acid hydrolysis and mechanical fibrillation is a low cost and environmentally friendly method of producing high thermally stable CNCs and CNFs.

the solid dicarboxylicate acids can produce carboxylate cellulose nanomaterials (CNs) with high thermal stability, longer length, and high crystallinity, while minimizing cellulose loss to sugar and generating high yield of carboxylated cellulosic FCSR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of highly recyclable organic acids in the production of carboxylated nanocellulose is a viable and sustainable approach to the green production of high thermal stability nanocelluloses.
highly recyclable solid acids can be used to produce thermally stable and highly carboxylated CNCs and CNFs from cellulosic fibers at low cost.

the use of solid dicarboxylical acids can produce high thermal stability and carboxyl content of CNCs and CNFs from both bleached and unbleached cellulosic fibers, and can be used in the future to produce low-cost, highly recyclable and biobased chemicals for cellulose nanomaterial production.
